solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Two days in A&E with another one tacked on

indicators.note: whatever is placed in something sits within it, so one piece goes inside the rest

blocks.note: the hospital department's letters, split around the insertion
D is the standard abbreviation for day, written twice
one more day, so one more D

explanation.surface: Someone spends two days in the emergency department, then has a third day added to their stay.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is the British hospital accident and emergency department. 'Another one' means another day, so a third D goes on the end: A(DD)E + D.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tacked on has been attached as an extra, which is the past participle meaning joined or appended.

clue.text: Unscrupulous US city travellers heading north

indicators.note: in a down entry, travelling north means reading from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: Los Angeles, abbreviated
the Roma are a traditionally travelling people

explanation.surface: Some shady travellers from an American city are on their way north.
explanation.walkthrough: LA plus ROMA, written upwards in the grid, gives AMORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unscrupulous ignores right and wrong, which is exactly having no moral principles at all.

clue.text: Work on kitchen renovation? I’m not helping!

blocks.note: first meaning: home improvement done by the householder, DIY
second meaning: what you snap at someone asking for your help

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a refusal to help a partner refit the kitchen; both halves name the same phrase, once as a noun for home improvement and once as a spoken retort.
explanation.definitionFit: DIY is the British term for amateur household building and decorating, and the same words form a curt brush-off.

clue.text: Dad loses out, a complete failure

indicators.note: something put out of place is disordered, so these letters must be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A father is beaten again and is judged a total flop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loses out' reads like a phrasal verb, but 'out' is the signal and 'loses' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead loss is an informal British idiom for a useless person or thing that completely fails.

clue.text: Geronimo, say, quickly capturing hearts

indicators.note: to capture is to take and hold, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: apace means swiftly
H is the card-playing abbreviation for the hearts suit

explanation.surface: Geronimo, the shout of a parachutist, rapidly wins people over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Geronimo' looks like the jumper's cry, but here it is the historical leader; 'say' marks him as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Geronimo was a famous nineteenth-century leader of that Native American people, so he is an example member.

clue.text: Animal suffered, by all accounts

indicators.note: accounts are things people tell, so we go by what is heard spoken

blocks.note: bore, as in endured, is the past tense of bear

explanation.surface: Reportedly, a certain creature went through a hard time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suffered' means bore, as in bore the pain, which sounds the same as the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A boar is a wild pig or uncastrated male pig, a straightforward example of an animal.

clue.text: Clandestine group surrounding English king

indicators.note: to surround is to enclose on all sides, so one piece goes around another

blocks.note: a sect is a group with shared beliefs
R for rex, Latin for king
E is the standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A shadowy faction gathers around an English monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The king's R goes in first and English E after it, so the inserted pair reads RE: SEC(RE)T.
explanation.definitionFit: Clandestine activity is kept hidden from others, the same sense as being kept confidential or private.

clue.text: Strange seeing OAP spying

indicators.note: something strange is out of its normal form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: How odd to find a pensioner snooping.
explanation.walkthrough: OAP stands for old-age pensioner, a British term for a retired person.
explanation.definitionFit: Spying used as a noun is the practice of gathering secret information, which is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Very large Mail cartoons reproduced

indicators.note: something reproduced is made anew, so these letters are put together in a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Daily Mail reprints its cartoons at an enormous size.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mail is a British newspaper, the Daily Mail; its capital letter disguises plain fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomical is an informal way of describing figures or sums so huge they seem to belong to space.

clue.text: Board needing a “yes” from Paris and Berlin

blocks.note: the French word for yes
the German word for yes, the same word shared

explanation.surface: A committee needs approval from both the French and German governments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' reads as a governing panel, but it is the spirit board, whose name really does join French and German words for yes.
explanation.definitionFit: A ouija board is a lettered board used in seances to receive supposed messages from spirits.

clue.text: Speaker at end of month will be a painter

indicators.note: placing something at the end of another means it follows it in the answer

blocks.note: the calendar abbreviation for December
an orator is a public speaker

explanation.surface: A lecturer booked for the end of the month turns out to be an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At end of month' sounds like a date, but it places the speaker after the abbreviated month.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the trade is 'painter and decorator', someone who paints and papers homes, so one names the other.

clue.text: Large ducks in the ladies perhaps

blocks.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
a duck is a score of zero in cricket, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Big ducks are waddling about in the women's restroom.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batter out for nought scores a duck; two of them give two Os. 'Perhaps' marks the ladies as one kind of toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: The ladies is the British name for a women's public toilet, and loo is an informal word for any toilet.

clue.text: Completed film a step too far?

blocks.note: something over is finished
to shoot a scene is to film it

explanation.surface: Having finished the movie, someone wonders whether it went too far.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition as loose: an overshoot is going past the intended point.
explanation.definitionFit: An overshoot is going beyond a target or limit, which is figuratively taking one step more than intended.

clue.text: Turn informer twice in NY prison

indicators.note: doing something twice means writing the same piece two times in a row

blocks.note: to sing is slang for confessing or informing on accomplices
the same slang word again, as the doubling asks

explanation.surface: A prisoner in a New York jail grasses on others twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: To sing, in criminal slang, is to tell the police what you know; doubled, it names the prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Sing Sing is a famous maximum-security correctional facility in Ossining, New York State, known from gangster films.

clue.text: New chair isn’t a religious person

indicators.note: something new has been remade, so these letters take on a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A newly appointed committee chair turns out not to be a believer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New chair' reads as a recently appointed leader, but 'New' is the signal for the following letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of the faith founded on Jesus is one specific example of a believer in a religion.

clue.text: Accost ’Arry, protecting fellow actor

indicators.note: to protect is to shelter within, so the words hold the answer inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone approaches Harry, said in a Cockney accent, to shield a colleague on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arry with a dropped H is Cockney for Harry; the dropped letter lets the answer run across the word break.
explanation.definitionFit: A co-star shares top billing in a film or play, so they are an actor working alongside another.

clue.text: Son abandoning extremely cold region for a warmer one?

indicators.note: to abandon something is to leave it behind, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: the frozen Russian region east of the Urals
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A son leaves a freezing land and heads somewhere warmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' stands for region, so the definition is a warmer region; the question mark admits it is defined by contrast.
explanation.definitionFit: Iberia is the peninsula of Spain and Portugal in southwest Europe, a hot and sunny region compared with Siberia.

clue.text: Idiot cancelled having heart transplant

indicators.note: a transplant swaps one organ for another, so the middle letter is replaced

blocks.note: an event called off is off

explanation.surface: A fool's operation was called off just as the heart transplant was due.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle F is swapped for a new letter, A, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An oaf is a clumsy, stupid person, a common synonym for a fool or blockhead.

clue.text: Unfinished state leaving you red-faced

indicators.note: something unfinished lacks its ending, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: the US state in the southeast

explanation.surface: An incomplete job for the government leaves you embarrassed and flushed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a condition, but it is a US state with its last letter cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: Florid describes a complexion that is ruddy or flushed, the same sense as having a reddened face.

clue.text: Tossing and turning, unlike princess awakened by a kiss?

definitions.text: unlike princess awakened by a kiss?

blocks.note: first meaning: restless in bed, unable to drop off

blocks.clueFragment: unlike princess awakened by a kiss?
blocks.note: second meaning: the opposite of Sleeping Beauty, who slept for a hundred years

explanation.walkthrough: The princess is Sleeping Beauty, woken by a prince's kiss after a century of sleep; someone unlike her never slept at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying awake tossing and turning describes a night without rest, the plain sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Treaty in the bag, one might say

indicators.note: what one might say is speech, so we go by what the words sound like

blocks.note: things in the bag have been packed

explanation.surface: A deal is as good as done, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the bag' looks like the idiom for a certain deal, which fits a treaty, but here it is literal: packed.
explanation.definitionFit: A pact is a formal agreement between parties or nations, a direct synonym for a treaty.

clue.text: Suffer tucking into certain curries?

indicators.note: tucking into food means eating inside it, so the letters sit within the words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of one word and start of the next

explanation.surface: Someone digs into a hot curry and pays for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucking into' is British slang for eating heartily, which fits the curries nicely.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a cost or penalty is to bring it upon yourself, so you suffer it as a consequence.

clue.text: Friendship to influence half of nation

indicators.note: half of a word means keeping only one of its two halves

blocks.note: to affect something is to influence it
the back three of its six letters

explanation.surface: Building friendships as a way to sway half the country.
explanation.walkthrough: A six-letter word halves neatly into three and three; the back half is kept here.
explanation.definitionFit: Affection is warm fondness or liking, the feeling that underlies a friendship, so it is a loose synonym.

clue.text: Frosty setter I start to dislike

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, which alone is kept

blocks.note: hair gel sets a hairstyle in place
taken as written
its opening letter

explanation.surface: The crossword setter admits to a chilly opening dislike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like the crossword compiler, as so often, but here it is something that sets hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelid is a literary word for icy cold, from the Latin for frost, so it matches frosty directly.
